results.title: Direct summand theorem
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $A$ be a regular commutative ring and let $B$ be a commutative $A$-algebra that is finitely generated as an $A$-module and on which $A$ acts faithfully (equivalently, the structure map $A \to B$ is injective). Then there is an $A$-linear map $\pi \colon B \to A$ with $\pi(a \cdot 1) = a$ for every $a \in A$; that is, $A$ is a direct summand of $B$ as an $A$-module.

results.title: Carmichael index
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a natural number $n$, the Carmichael index $N(n)$ is the number of integers $a$ with $0 \le a \le n - 1$ and $a^n \equiv a \pmod{n}$.

results.title: The Carmichael index of 1
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The Carmichael index of $1$ is $N(1) = 1$.

results.title: The Carmichael indices of 4 and 66
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The Carmichael index satisfies $N(4) = 2$ and $N(66) = 24$.

results.title: Product formula for the Carmichael index
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $n \ge 2$ and, for each prime $p$ dividing $n$, let $p^{e_p}$ be the largest power of $p$ dividing $n$. Then the Carmichael index of $n$ is $N(n) = \prod_p \bigl(N(n; p^{e_p}) + 1\bigr)$, the product running over the primes $p$ dividing $n$, where $N(n; p^{e_p})$ is the number of units of $\mathbb{Z}/p^{e_p}\mathbb{Z}$ whose multiplicative order divides $\gcd(p - 1, n/p^{e_p} - 1)$.

results.title: The Carmichael index of $n$ is never $n - 1$
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every positive integer $n$, the Carmichael index $N(n)$, the number of integers $a$ with $0 \le a \le n - 1$ and $a^n \equiv a \pmod{n}$, is not equal to $n - 1$.

results.title: Viviani's theorem
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $A$, $B$, $C$ be points of the Euclidean plane $\mathbb{R}^2$ with $AB = BC = CA$, and let $P$ be a point of the interior of the convex hull of $\lbrace A, B, C \rbrace$. Then the sum of the distances from $P$ to the lines $AB$, $BC$ and $CA$ equals the distance from $A$ to the line $BC$, the altitude of the triangle.

results.title: Viviani's theorem with a positive side length
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $A$, $B$, $C$ be points of the Euclidean plane $\mathbb{R}^2$ with $AB = BC = CA$ and $AB > 0$, and let $P$ be a point of the interior of the convex hull of $\lbrace A, B, C \rbrace$. Then the sum of the distances from $P$ to the lines $AB$, $BC$ and $CA$ equals the distance from $A$ to the line $BC$, the altitude of the triangle.

results.title: Cells of a Ferrers board
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a list $b = (b_1, \ldots, b_n)$ of natural numbers, the cells of the Ferrers board with column heights $b$ are the pairs $(i, r)$ of natural numbers with $i < n$ and $r < b_{i+1}$; columns and rows are numbered from $0$, so column $i$ has height $b_{i+1}$.

results.title: The board $(1, 1, 2, 4)$ has eight cells
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The Ferrers board with column heights $(1, 1, 2, 4)$, the board $B_1$ of Figure 2, has exactly $8$ cells.

results.title: File placements
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A file placement on the Ferrers board with column heights $b$ is a set of cells of the board no two of which lie in the same column.

results.title: Level rook placements
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $m$ be a natural number and let $B$ be the board with column heights $b_1, \dots, b_n$, rows numbered from $0$, where row $r$ lies in level $\lfloor r/m \rfloor$ (every row lies in level $0$ when $m = 0$). An $m$-level rook placement on $B$ is a file placement on $B$, that is a set of cells of $B$ with no two in the same column, that has no two cells in the same level.

results.title: Level rook number
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $m$ and $k$ be natural numbers and let $B$ be the board with column heights $b_1, \dots, b_n$, with rows numbered from $0$, where row $r$ lies in level $\lfloor r/m \rfloor$ (every row lies in level $0$ when $m = 0$). The $k$-th $m$-level rook number $r_{k,m}(B)$ is the number of $m$-level rook placements on $B$ with exactly $k$ cells, that is, of sets of $k$ cells of $B$ with no two in the same column and no…

results.title: The $m$-falling factorial
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For an integer $x$ and natural numbers $k$ and $m$, the $m$-falling factorial is the integer $x\downarrow_{k,m} = \prod_{i=0}^{k-1} (x - mi) = x(x-m)\cdots(x-(k-1)m)$, which is $1$ for $k = 0$.

results.title: The value $1\downarrow_{3,2} = 3$
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The $2$-falling factorial of $1$ with three factors is $1\downarrow_{3,2} = 1 \cdot (1 - 2) \cdot (1 - 4) = 3$.

results.title: The $m$-weight of a file placement
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a natural number $m$ and a finite set $F$ of cells $(i, j)$ (column $i$, row $j$), let $f_j$ be the number of cells of $F$ in row $j$. The $m$-weight of $F$ is $\mathrm{wt}_m(F) = \prod_j 1\downarrow_{f_j, m}$, the product over the rows $j$ that contain a cell of $F$, where $x\downarrow_{k, m} = \prod_{i < k} (x - m i)$ is the $m$-falling factorial.

results.title: The $3$-weight of the placement of Figure 4
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The file placement $F$ consisting of the cells $(0, 1)$, $(1, 1)$, $(2, 3)$, $(3, 3)$ and $(4, 3)$, written as (column, row) and numbered from $0$, has two cells in the second row and three in the fourth, and its $3$-weight is $\mathrm{wt}_3(F) = -20$.

results.title: Weighted file placement numbers
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a board $B$ given by a list of column heights and for $m, k \in \mathbb{N}$, the $k$-th $m$-weighted file placement number of $B$ is the integer $f_{k,m}(B) = \sum_F \mathrm{wt}_m(F)$, where $F$ runs over the file placements on $B$ with exactly $k$ cells and $\mathrm{wt}_m(F)$ is the $m$-weight of $F$.

results.title: Singleton boards
results.caption: Definition

results.title: Families in which no member is a union of other members
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A family $F$ of finite sets is union-free over its subfamilies if no member $A \in F$ is the union of a nonempty subfamily of $F$ that does not contain $A$.

results.title: Union-free family
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A family $F$ of subsets of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ is union-free if there are no pairwise distinct $A, B, C \in F$ with $A \cup B = C$.

results.title: Maximum size of a union-free family
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a natural number $n$, the largest size $|F|$ of a union-free family $F$ of subsets of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$.

results.title: Erdős Problem 447, first question
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The assertion that the maximum size of a union-free family of subsets of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ is $o(2^n)$ as $n \to \infty$.

results.title: Erdős Problem 447, second question
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The assertion that, for every real $\varepsilon > 0$ and all sufficiently large $n$, the maximum size of a union-free family of subsets of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ is at most $(1 + \varepsilon)\binom{n}{\lfloor n/2 \rfloor}$; that is, it is at most $(1 + o(1))\binom{n}{\lfloor n/2 \rfloor}$.

results.title: Union-free families have vanishing density (Erdős Problem 447)
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The maximum size of a union-free family of subsets of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ is $o(2^n)$ as $n \to \infty$.

results.title: Kleitman's bound for union-free families (Erdős Problem 447)
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every real $\varepsilon > 0$ and all sufficiently large $n$, the maximum size of a union-free family of subsets of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ is at most $(1 + \varepsilon)\binom{n}{\lfloor n/2 \rfloor}$; that is, it is at most $(1 + o(1))\binom{n}{\lfloor n/2 \rfloor}$.

results.title: The GISTIC permutation null is the law of a sum of independent per-sample draws
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: (Mermel et al. 2011): the probability of the score `g` is the fraction of the `M ^ S` marker choices with that score, whatever the marker `m`.

results.title: GISTIC null with no samples is a point mass at zero
results.caption: Theorem

results.title: Convolution step
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Adding sample `S` convolves the null of the first `S` samples with the empirical law of the new sample, `P_{S+1}(g) = ∑_v (1 / M) P_S(g - x_S(v))`.

results.title: Window minimum over consecutive markers

results.title: GeneGISTIC null

results.summary: GeneGISTIC null (Mermel et al. 2011): permuting the per-sample minima of all running windows of `n + 1` markers gives, at every window `i`, the law of a sum of independent draws of one window minimum per sample.
